ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Word came that someone they knew before the colony has died, far away. It fades in a few days. A wake that evening or a day to themselves when the news comes makes it lighter than being sent straight back to work.
A frost killed the crops they had been growing. It fades within a week. When a frost is coming, sending hands to bring in what's ripe saves both the crop and the grower's mood.
Something they cared about or answered for is gone: an animal taken in the night, a keepsake carried off down the road, a stake lost at the gambler's table. It fades in a few days.

The council did something they found heartless: shut the gate on people in need, or hunted animals running from a fire. Only the kind feel it, and it fades in a few days. A kinder answer next time keeps it from coming back.
Someone was called home: they stayed and said no to their family, or they went, and the others miss them. It fades within a week; evenings with friends help in the meantime.
The apprentice they were teaching left before the season was out. It fades in a few days. A long talk with the youngster when trouble comes can keep them at the bench.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: A good turn from a Rimfolk event or a story: a keepsake bought back, a family sheltered, an apprentice taught, a town helped through a fever. Most of these give something other than a mood (pride, trust, practice), and they come from the answers the council gives.
